name: Simple Vegetable Pulao
instructions: Rinse 1 cup of uncooked rice. Dice 1 carrot and 1 small onion.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a saucepan. Add 1 teaspoon of cumin seeds, then the onion. Cook until softened.
Add the carrot and half a cup of peas. Cook for 3 minutes.
Add the rice, 2 cups of water, and half a teaspoon of salt.
Bring to a boil, cover, and reduce the heat to low. Cook for 15–18 minutes, until the rice is tender and the water is absorbed.
Turn off the heat, rest covered for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.

name: Simple Kimchi Fried Rice
instructions: Use 2 cups of cooked rice and chop 1 cup of kimchi.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a frying pan. Add the kimchi and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the rice and 1 teaspoon of soy sauce. Stir-fry until hot throughout.
In a separate pan, fry 2 eggs until the whites and yolks are set.
Divide the rice between two bowls and top each with an egg.

name: Simple Onigiri
instructions: Prepare 2 cups of warm, cooked Japanese short-grain rice.
Wet your hands with clean water and lightly sprinkle them with salt.
Divide the rice into 4 portions.
Gently shape each portion into a triangle or ball.
Wrap each rice ball with a strip of nori and serve.

name: Cheese Omelet
instructions: Beat 2 eggs with a small pinch of salt.
Melt 1 teaspoon of butter in a small nonstick pan over medium-low heat.
Pour in the eggs. Gently move the cooked edges toward the center, letting uncooked egg flow underneath.
When the top is almost set, add a quarter cup of shredded cheese to one half.
Fold the omelet over the cheese and cook until the egg is fully set and the cheese melts.

name: Simple Chicken Biryani
instructions: Mix 500 g boneless chicken pieces with half a cup of plain yogurt, 1 tablespoon each of minced ginger and garlic, 1 tablespoon of biryani masala, a quarter teaspoon of turmeric, half a teaspoon of chili powder, and half a teaspoon of salt. Refrigerate for 20 minutes.
Rinse 1.5 cups of basmati rice and soak for 20 minutes. Drain.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a heavy saucepan. Add 1 large sliced onion and cook until golden.
Add the chicken with its marinade. Cook over medium heat for 12–15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add a quarter cup each of chopped mint and coriander. Stir in the drained rice and 2.5 cups of hot water.
Bring to a gentle boil. Cover tightly and cook over low heat for about 18–20 minutes, until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed. Add a little hot water if needed.
Check that the thickest chicken pieces reach 165°F (74°C). Turn off the heat and rest covered for 10 minutes before gently mixing.

name: Chicken 65
instructions: Cut 500 g boneless chicken into small, evenly sized pieces.

Mix with 3 tablespoons of plain yogurt, 1 teaspoon each of minced ginger and garlic, 1 teaspoon of chili powder, a quarter teaspoon of turmeric, and half a teaspoon of salt. Refrigerate for 20 minutes.
Mix in 2 tablespoons of cornstarch and 1 tablespoon of rice flour to coat the chicken.
Heat about 1 cm of oil in a heavy frying pan over medium heat. Carefully add the chicken in small batches.
Fry, turning occasionally, until golden and the center of the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C). Remove and drain.
In a separate pan, heat 1 teaspoon of oil. Add 8–10 washed and thoroughly dried curry leaves and cook briefly; they may splutter.
Toss the chicken with the curry leaves and 1 tablespoon of lemon juice, then serve.

name: Indo-Chinese Egg Fried Rice
instructions: Prepare 2 cups of cooked rice, 2 beaten eggs, 1 finely diced carrot, 2 chopped spring onions, and 2 minced garlic cloves.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a large frying pan. Add the eggs and scramble until fully set. Transfer to a plate.
Add another teaspoon of oil. Cook the garlic and carrot for 3–4 minutes.
Add the rice and 1 tablespoon of soy sauce. Stir-fry until hot throughout.
Return the eggs to the pan. Add the spring onions and a quarter teaspoon of pepper.
Mix well and serve hot.

name: Spinach Dal
instructions: Rinse three-quarters of a cup of toor dal. Place in a saucepan with 3 cups of water and a quarter teaspoon of turmeric.
Bring to a boil, then simmer partially covered for 25–35 minutes until soft. Add more hot water if needed.
Wash and chop 3 cups of spinach. Chop 1 small onion, 1 tomato, and 3 garlic cloves.
In a separate pan, heat 1 tablespoon of oil. Add half a teaspoon of cumin seeds, followed by the onion and garlic. Cook until softened.
Add the tomato and half a teaspoon of chili powder. Cook for 5 minutes.
Add the spinach and cook until wilted.
Stir the spinach mixture into the cooked dal. Add half a teaspoon of salt and water as needed for your preferred consistency.
Simmer for 5 minutes and serve.

name: Palak Paneer
instructions: Wash 250 g spinach. Blanch in boiling water for 1–2 minutes, then drain and rinse with cold water.
Blend the spinach with a little clean water into a puree.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a saucepan. Add half a teaspoon of cumin seeds and 1 finely chopped onion. Cook until softened.
Add 1 teaspoon each of minced ginger and garlic. Cook for 1 minute.
Add 1 finely chopped tomato and cook until soft.
Stir in the spinach puree, half a teaspoon of garam masala, and half a teaspoon of salt. Gently simmer for 5 minutes.
Add 250 g cubed paneer and 2 tablespoons of cream. Add a little water if needed.
Gently simmer for another 3–5 minutes and serve.

name: Spinach and Garlic Rice
instructions: Prepare 2 cups of cooked rice. The listed time assumes the rice is already cooked.
Wash and chop 2 cups of spinach. Finely chop 4 garlic cloves.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a large pan. Add half a teaspoon of cumin seeds.
Add the garlic and cook over medium-low heat for about 1 minute without burning it.
Add the spinach and cook for 3–4 minutes until wilted.
Add the cooked rice, a quarter teaspoon of pepper, and a quarter teaspoon of salt.
Mix gently and cook until the rice is hot throughout, then serve.

name: Simple Spinach Curry
instructions: Wash and chop 300 g spinach. Chop 1 small onion, 1 tomato, and 3 garlic cloves.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a saucepan. Add half a teaspoon of cumin seeds.
Add the onion and garlic. Cook until the onion softens.
Add the tomato, a quarter teaspoon of turmeric, half a teaspoon of chili powder, and half a teaspoon of salt.
Cook for 5 minutes until the tomato softens.
Add the spinach in batches, stirring as it wilts.
Add a quarter cup of water and simmer for 5–8 minutes until the spinach is tender. Serve.

name: Indo-Chinese Chicken Fried Rice
instructions: Prepare 2 cups of cooked rice. Cut 250 g boneless chicken into small pieces. Dice 1 carrot, chop 2 spring onions, and mince 2 garlic cloves.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a large frying pan. Add the chicken and cook, stirring, until its center reaches 165°F (74°C). Transfer to a clean plate.
Add another teaspoon of oil. Cook the garlic and carrot for 3–4 minutes.
Add the rice and 1 tablespoon of soy sauce. Stir-fry until hot throughout.
Return the cooked chicken to the pan. Add the spring onions and a quarter teaspoon of pepper.
Mix well, heat everything through, and serve.

name: Oven Chicken Tikka
instructions: Cut 500 g boneless chicken into evenly sized pieces, about 3 cm wide.

Mix half a cup of plain yogurt with 1 tablespoon of lemon juice, 1 teaspoon each of minced ginger, minced garlic, garam masala, ground cumin, and chili powder, a quarter teaspoon of turmeric, half a teaspoon of salt, and 1 tablespoon of oil.
Coat the chicken in the marinade and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a baking tray with baking paper.
Arrange the chicken in a single layer with space between the pieces.
Bake for about 18–25 minutes, turning halfway through, until the thickest pieces reach 165°F (74°C).
Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

name: Carrot Kurma
instructions: Slice 4 medium carrots, chop 1 onion and 1 tomato, and mince 1 teaspoon each of ginger and garlic.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a saucepan. Add half a teaspoon of cumin seeds, then the onion. Cook until softened.
Add the ginger and garlic. Stir for 1 minute.
Add the tomato, a quarter teaspoon of turmeric, 1 teaspoon of garam masala, and half a teaspoon of salt. Cook for 5 minutes.
Add the carrots and half a cup of water. Cover and simmer for 10–15 minutes until the carrots are tender.
Stir in three-quarters of a cup of coconut milk. Gently simmer for 5 minutes and serve.

name: Paneer Tikka Masala
instructions: Mix 300 g cubed paneer with a quarter cup of plain yogurt, half a teaspoon each of garam masala and chili powder, and a quarter teaspoon of salt. Refrigerate for 15 minutes.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a nonstick pan. Cook the paneer in a single layer, turning gently until lightly browned. Set aside.
In a saucepan, heat 1 tablespoon of oil. Add 1 finely chopped onion and cook until golden.
Add 1 teaspoon each of minced ginger and garlic. Cook for 1 minute.
Add 1 cup of pureed tomato, half a teaspoon each of garam masala and chili powder, and a quarter teaspoon of salt. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Add a quarter cup of water and a quarter cup of cream. Stir in the paneer and gently simmer for 5 minutes.

name: Simple Butter Chicken
instructions: Mix 500 g boneless chicken pieces with a quarter cup of plain yogurt, 1 teaspoon each of minced ginger and garlic, half a teaspoon each of garam masala and chili powder, and a quarter teaspoon of salt. Refrigerate for 20 minutes.
Melt 1 tablespoon of butter in a large pan over medium heat. Add the chicken with its marinade and cook for 8–10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add 1.5 cups of pureed tomato, half a teaspoon each of garam masala and chili powder, and a quarter teaspoon of salt.
Simmer gently for 15–20 minutes, stirring occasionally. Add a little water if the sauce becomes too thick.
Check that the thickest chicken pieces reach 165°F (74°C).
Stir in a third of a cup of cream and 1 tablespoon of butter. Gently heat for 2 minutes and serve.

name: Paneer Bhurji
instructions: Crumble 250 g paneer. Finely chop 1 onion and 1 tomato.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a pan. Add half a teaspoon of cumin seeds, then the onion. Cook until softened.
Add 1 teaspoon of minced ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomato, a quarter teaspoon of turmeric, half a teaspoon of chili powder, and half a teaspoon of salt. Cook until the tomato softens.
Add the crumbled paneer. Stir gently and cook for 3–4 minutes.
Finish with 2 tablespoons of chopped coriander and serve.

name: Paneer 65
instructions: Cut 300 g paneer into cubes.
Mix 3 tablespoons of plain yogurt with 1 teaspoon each of minced ginger, minced garlic, and chili powder, plus half a teaspoon of salt.
Gently coat the paneer in the mixture. Add 2 tablespoons of cornstarch and 1 tablespoon of rice flour, then mix carefully.
Heat about 1 cm of oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Shallow-fry the paneer in batches, turning gently until golden. Remove and drain.
In a separate pan, heat 1 teaspoon of oil. Briefly cook 8–10 washed and thoroughly dried curry leaves; they may splutter.
Add the paneer and 1 tablespoon of lemon juice. Toss gently and serve.

name: Indo-Chinese Paneer Fried Rice
instructions: Prepare 2 cups of cooked rice, 200 g cubed paneer, 1 finely diced carrot, 2 chopped spring onions, and 2 minced garlic cloves.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a large pan. Lightly brown the paneer, then transfer it to a plate.
Add another teaspoon of oil. Cook the garlic and carrot for 3–4 minutes.
Add the rice and 1 tablespoon of soy sauce. Stir-fry until hot throughout.
Return the paneer to the pan. Add the spring onions and a quarter teaspoon of pepper.
Mix gently, heat everything through, and serve.

name: Indo-Chinese Paneer Manchurian
instructions: Coat 300 g paneer cubes with 2 tablespoons of cornstarch and 1 tablespoon of water.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a nonstick pan. Cook the paneer, turning gently until golden. Set aside.
Add 1 teaspoon of oil to the pan. Cook 1 teaspoon each of minced garlic and ginger for 30 seconds.
Add 1 small diced onion and 1 diced bell pepper. Stir-fry for 3–4 minutes.
Add 1 tablespoon of soy sauce, 2 tablespoons of ketchup, 1 teaspoon of vinegar, and half a cup of water.
Mix 1 teaspoon of cornstarch with 1 tablespoon of cold water. Stir into the sauce and simmer until thickened.
Add the paneer, toss gently, and heat for 2 minutes before serving.

name: Indo-Chinese Chicken Manchurian
instructions: Cut 400 g boneless chicken into small, evenly sized pieces. Coat with 2 tablespoons of cornstarch and 1 tablespoon of soy sauce.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a large nonstick pan. Cook the chicken in batches, turning until browned and its center reaches 165°F (74°C). Transfer to a clean plate.
Add 1 teaspoon of oil to the pan. Cook 1 teaspoon each of minced garlic and ginger for 30 seconds.
Add 1 small diced onion and 1 diced bell pepper. Stir-fry for 3–4 minutes.
Add 1 tablespoon of soy sauce, 2 tablespoons of ketchup, 1 teaspoon of vinegar, and half a cup of water.
Mix 1 teaspoon of cornstarch with 1 tablespoon of cold water. Stir into the sauce and simmer until thickened.
Return the cooked chicken to the pan. Stir and heat everything through before serving.
